common_prompt: Create ONE entirely new 4:5 vertical SanctusArs artwork for the verified Catholic Gospel. The supplied images are references for color relationships, mostly smooth matte finish, restrained edge texture and degree of omission only, not for composition or character design. The independently written scene description, derived from today's verified passage and quotation, determines camera axis, figure placement, gesture and symbolic form. Never copy the references' scene, camera angle, large color-field boundaries, silhouette, persons, faces, gestures, garments or symbols. A visually polished result that resembles a reference face or layout is a failed candidate. The whole Gospel episode supplies context, but the short quoted sentence supplies the single visual idea. This image accompanies the short post: it need not retell the whole passage. At first glance one gaze, pause, gesture, distance or spatial relation should connect to the quotation; allow the viewer to infer everything else. All three candidates must simplify; if removing a figure, prop or wall leaves the quoted relation clear, remove it. Choose camera axis and focal alignment for each candidate from the quoted relation, not from a fixed list or quota. Compare the three scenes together: do not offer three near-identical side views that differ only in distance. A frontal or intimate view can carry a decisive word; a wider view can preserve context that makes a relationship legible. An overhead view may suggest an unseen divine gaze when the passage supports it. A reflection in water, a person seen between others or another partly obscured viewpoint is welcome only when it deepens this particular Gospel meaning, never as a novelty effect. B is the most simplified candidate that still communicates the essential relation; retain enough context when further removal would make it cryptic. Compose a singular contemporary sacred artwork from a few large asymmetrical, mostly smooth matte color fields, purposeful overlaps, one legible human anchor where needed, and substantial active space. Keep fine grain or haze only at a small meaningful transition, never as an all-over filter. Keep the established simplicity and abstraction, but slightly reduce geometric stylization. Favor natural, gently irregular contours and flowing garment shapes over ruler-straight divisions, repeated triangles or polygonal facets, especially in faces, hands and clothing. Keep large clear color fields and purposeful edges; use straight lines where the subject needs them, not as the default abstraction. Do not replace every edge with a decorative curve, blur the whole image, add detail, or introduce painterly brushwork or extra texture. Cobalt blue, deep plum, muted sage and ivory are a recognizable family, not four colors that must all appear each day. Use only the colors the scene needs; avoid purple dominance, orange warmth and cold monochrome. Cobalt is not a signal of night: in passages without a stated time, daylight and open-air brightness are welcome. Preserve a restrained sense of the sacred through withheld space, selective light and scale. Apply only the per-person sacred_light_policy supplied for visible subjects; do not infer light intensity from the generic word sacred or from reference images. Use sacred_light only to locate that permitted light naturally. Ordinary daylight or a bright wall alone is not the localized cue. No isolated glowing spot on collarbone, throat, chest or skin; no hard disc, metal hoop, neon outline, decorative laser beam, glitter or all-over glow. If sacred_subjects is empty, invent neither a sacred figure nor a halo. Human forms share the same illustrated language as the space: hands and eyes remain coherent wherever visible, never photographic, faceless, distorted or toy-like. This is modern art with a Gospel anchor, not a full Bible-story diagram, vintage oil painting, textured canvas, picture book, stock digital illustration, vector icon or generic abstract poster. No heavy brushstrokes, impasto, paper fibers, grunge, repeated texture, text, logo, signature, border or reserved text area. Generate fresh from scratch; never edit an existing candidate. Scene illumination has a separate purpose and is governed by scene_light_policy. It must not overwrite the identity-linked sacred_light_policy; any stronger event light requires the declared scene basis. For an angel, use simplified wings as the identifying feature and only the existing subtle local light. Never add an angel ring, floating ellipse, circular luminous outline or partial ring-shaped arc behind or above the head. Let any head-edge light diffuse without outlining a ring. When the composition crops out wings, do not insert a ring as a substitute.

A.direction: A / WIDE BUT EDITED DOWN. Show the quoted relation from a wider position, not the full cast or chronology. Let the passage decide whether a high, frontal or lateral vantage best shows the relationship. Keep enough spatial context when removing it would make the quoted idea unclear; a wide image is more than a small person in empty space. Use the scale of figures that makes the relationship immediately legible, with broad quiet color fields doing much of the work. Remove domestic inventory, extra actors and architecture that merely explains the story. This candidate may suggest daylight even when cobalt is present. Do not recreate any reference path, doorway or pose.

B.direction: B / RADICAL MINIMUM. This must be the most dramatically simplified interpretation that still carries the quoted Gospel sentence. Use a close crop or near-abstract arrangement with one legible human anchor when the quoted relation needs one: a listening posture, a partial face, a restrained gesture or a small silhouette oriented toward an unseen presence. If the verse itself gives a concrete metaphor such as a stone, let that single form carry the relation without inserting a person. Keep two or three large quiet color fields and at most one small accent. Make this a dramatic minimum: create bold tension from a single scale difference, a decisive meeting of two large fields with subject-led contours, or a controlled light-dark transition tied to the quoted relation. The viewer should feel the reversal immediately while the image remains spare. Preserve one unmistakable concrete visual cue to the verified quoted line or the verified central Gospel event; after reading the short post, the viewer must be able to name what in this image evokes that Gospel. A beautiful arrangement of color and light with no such cue fails, even if strikingly minimal. Do not add more actors, props, theatrical beams, particles or decorative effects for drama. Omit the room, table, utensils, supporting cast and explanatory props unless one is indispensable to this particular verse. Let the viewer complete the unseen encounter. Do not repeat the reference's Mary, Jesus, hand, dress or blue-plum divide; find a fresh form for today's words. Preserve the Gospel's emotional relation without becoming a generic abstract poster. No conventional portrait, hand reaching at camera or decorative detail.

C.direction: C / DISTINCT VIEWPOINT, EQUALLY SPARE. Find an interpretive vantage that A and B do not already provide, revealing another Gospel-grounded meaning through who sees, misses, receives or chooses in response to the quoted relation. A different camera angle alone is not a new interpretation. It could look down, directly face the subject, follow a line of sight, see a reflection, or glimpse the subject between people, only if that perspective serves the quoted sentence. Do not settle for another side profile with a different crop or force an unusual angle just to be different. Let one occlusion, scale shift or cropped gesture reveal the quoted relation. Keep the image as edited down as A, with no tableau, period set or illustrative inventory. It must be a distinct interpretation of the quoted idea, not a recolor or crop of A or B. Do not recreate either reference's scene or figures.

occasion_prompt: Create ONE entirely new 4:5 vertical SanctusArs artwork honoring the commemorated saint or sacred figure named in the occasion data. The person being remembered is the unmistakable visual subject. A saint day honors that person, so do not depict a distant figure inside a wide Gospel-event tableau. Use a person-centered medium portrait, a meaningful minimal detail, or a substantially different view, including a spacious full-figure composition where the person remains visually substantial. Do not restrict all three options to nearby bust portraits. Choose camera axis and focal alignment to honor the particular person and their verified meaning, not to fill a fixed set of overhead, frontal and wide views. A frontal or close view often gives a feast-day portrait the needed presence; use it when it serves this person. Compare the three artworks and avoid repeating the same lateral profile. An overhead, reflected or partly obscured view is possible only if the saint remains recognizable and the viewpoint adds meaning. For a joint feast, give the commemorated figures balanced presence instead of making one dominant by accident. The verified Gospel quote and scripture_relation may inform one subtle gesture or attitude, but they are secondary to the occasion's verified identity, meaning and sourced symbols. Do not invent a biography scene, quotation, costume detail or attribute that the sources do not support. Only when a source-backed attribute helps identify this particular saint, introduce at most one small, quiet symbolic element in this candidate. Do not force the symbol into every option. It may recur in a meaningful close-up of the same gesture or attribute, with consistent shape and clothing. Remove it if it draws attention before the person, adds clutter, turns cute, or falsely implies a documented biographical event. Omit supporting cast and historical scenery unless indispensable. The supplied images are references for palette, mostly smooth matte finish, restrained edge texture and degree of omission only, not for composition or character design. The independently written scene description, derived from this particular person and the verified occasion, determines camera axis, figure placement, gesture and symbolic form. Never copy the references' people, faces, poses, hands, garments, scene, camera angle or color-field boundaries. A visually polished result that resembles a reference face or layout is a failed candidate. Compose a singular contemporary sacred artwork from a few large asymmetric mostly smooth matte color fields. Keep the established simplicity and abstraction, but slightly reduce geometric stylization. Favor natural, gently irregular contours and flowing garment shapes over ruler-straight divisions, repeated triangles or polygonal facets, especially in faces, hands and clothing. Keep large clear color fields and purposeful edges; use straight lines where the subject needs them, not as the default abstraction. Do not replace every edge with a decorative curve, blur the whole image, add detail, or introduce painterly brushwork or extra texture. Cobalt blue, deep plum, restrained sage and ivory are a color family, not a required four-color set; daylight is welcome and purple must not dominate. Keep fine grain or haze only at one meaningful edge. Apply only the per-person sacred_light_policy supplied for visible subjects; do not infer light intensity from the generic word sacred or from reference images. Use sacred_light only to locate that permitted light naturally. Ordinary daylight or a bright wall alone is not the localized cue. No isolated glowing spot on collarbone, throat, chest or skin; no hard disc, metal hoop, neon outline, decorative laser beam, glitter or all-over glow. If sacred_subjects is empty, invent neither a sacred figure nor a halo. Faces and hands must be coherent and illustrated in the same language as the space, never photographic, erased or distorted. Preserve recognizable human presence while simplifying secondary detail. No vintage oil painting, heavy brushwork, picture-book illustration, stock digital portrait, generic abstract poster, text, logo, signature, border or reserved text area. Generate fresh from scratch; never edit an existing candidate. Treat the options as a possible multi-image post: each pairing must add new visible information and a distinct experience. A and C must not repeat a bowed head, similar silhouette and color-field arrangement with only small camera or crop changes. B must isolate a specific meaningful action, expression or attribute; arbitrarily bisecting a face is not meaningful abstraction. Same person and wardrobe do not mean the same pose or layout. Scene illumination has a separate purpose and is governed by scene_light_policy. It must not overwrite the identity-linked sacred_light_policy; any stronger event light requires the declared scene basis. For an angel, use simplified wings as the identifying feature and only the existing subtle local light. Never add an angel ring, floating ellipse, circular luminous outline or partial ring-shaped arc behind or above the head. Let any head-edge light diffuse without outlining a ring. When the composition crops out wings, do not insert a ring as a substitute.

A.direction: A / PERSON-CENTERED PORTRAIT. Compose the commemorated saint in a restrained medium or half-figure view, frontal, three-quarter or another angle that gives this person the strongest presence, large enough that face, posture and one meaningful verified attribute or gesture read immediately on a phone. Use broad active space around the person, but never shrink the saint into a tiny figure or make landscape and narrative setting the subject. No group of bystanders or reenacted episode.

B.direction: B / MEANINGFUL DETAIL, RADICAL MINIMUM. Choose a specific action, expression or verified attribute belonging to this person and show why it deserves closer attention. A hand gently advancing one rosary bead, an attentive face, or another meaningful contact may carry the idea. Retain the complete readable gesture or expression while omitting the surroundings. Do not arbitrarily halve a face or crop away the very feature carrying meaning. This can be a newly generated close view of a detail established in A, with the same garment and prop, but must reveal something the broader portrait cannot. Use two or three broad quiet fields and a subtle local glow; make this the simplest option. No extra explanatory objects or decorative fragments.

C.direction: C / COMPLEMENTARY VIEW. Show the same commemorated person from a substantially different visual and contemplative position than A. If A is a bowed half-portrait, do not make another bowed half-portrait with a slightly higher camera. A spacious full-figure frontal view with a different gaze and posture, a true overhead composition, or another meaning-driven perspective is possible. Keep the person substantial and recognizable; do not turn this into a distant landscape or event tableau. Choose the view for the occasion, not a fixed camera quota. The silhouette, focal action and arrangement must visibly differ from A/B so posting two images adds value. Omit setting and props that do not contribute.

light_profiles.divine_halo: For this divine person only, a clearly visible softly diffused halo behind the head is permitted. Keep soft edges and the figure legible, not a hard gold disc or theatrical beam. This permission never applies to another person in the image.
light_profiles.subtle: This is NOT a divine person. Keep the face and human presence primary. Add only a low-contrast, narrow, softly feathered trace at ONE head contour or natural garment edge. No luminous disc or broad bright cloud behind the head, no radiant corona, no glowing body. On a phone the trace may be noticed on second inspection but must not attract attention before the face. If the halo reads as a strong separate light source, it is excessive and fails review. Do not amplify it to prove that light is present.

scene_light_profiles.ambient: Use quiet scene illumination sufficient for the gaze, gesture and spatial relation to read. Do not add a dramatic shaft, portal or spotlight simply because the subject is religious. Keep separate from each person’s sacred_light_policy. Minimal form and empty space remain the main composition.
scene_light_profiles.dramatic: Use the declared source, focus and basis to make ONE decisive light-dark relationship express this verified event or contemplative turning point. Scene light does not upgrade any person’s identity or permitted halo intensity: Mary, saints and angels remain under their own restrained sacred_light_policy, even in a miracle. External light may illuminate faces and clothing naturally without making the person an emitting source. Do not disguise a broad head-centered glow or body aura as environmental light. Concentrate drama at the event, threshold, distance or action identified by focus, not an unrelated patch of skin. When the verified passage explicitly describes supernatural radiance, portray only that sourced manifestation; do not use it to imply a saint is divine. When light is an artistic metaphor rather than a described fact, preserve that distinction in basis and do not invent a miracle. Use contrast, scale, withheld illumination and a single light edge before adding shapes. Keep large quiet fields and readable figures; no repeated rays, glitter, particles, lens flares, neon, multiple competing focal lights or cinematic effects inventory. Not every miracle needs luminous effects and not all A/B/C options need dramatic lighting.
